about: The tillr backend policy: per backend, the adapter program and the model data staging hands it, plus the tick's default backend and the ordered preference a failover walks. The adapters read none of this file and carry no default of their own; the driver reads it at staging and puts the values on the adapter's argv, which is why a retired model id is fixed here in one line. No model id in this file may be copied into the tillr tree (tools/tillr*): that tree ships publicly and names no model vendor. Design: docs/design/tillr-muse-backend.md, sections 2, 7 and 9. Switching which models work today is this file and nothing else: `default_backend` names the one that answers, `preference` is the order a failover walks, `seats` maps each role an item may ask for (design, build, review, scout) to the backend that fills it, `overrides` routes one named item to another backend, and a backend that is unreachable stays declared so its machinery keeps its tests and comes back by naming it here again. What the owner selected on 2026-11-14: `pi` runs the DeepSeek floor row for every dispatch, and that row's own `openrouter_routing` (tag-personal's `model_facts.deepseek-floor-1017`) is what picks the serving upstream, so the route is chosen in the profile and NOT here -- `:ionstream/flex` as of this line, which is why this file names no upstream. The `models` rotation list is gone with that selection: the seven route rows still exist for an interactive session, but a lane draws no route. `pi-designer` is the same adapter on the Carbon row, and it is the seat layer's seam: an item asks for the design seat and `seats` points it here, so changing which model designs -- or moving the seat to another backend -- is a line here and never a change to an item. `agy` and `muse` are DECLARED AND NOT DISPATCHED TO: muse because every model began refusing on 2026-11-12 (the Meta subscription lapsed, so a `muse model-profile show` exit 0 is not evidence of access), and agy because the owner is developing that backend by running tillr's own items through it later rather than by cutting real work over to it now. Neither is in `preference`, so neither is reached by a failover and neither is reached by accident.
